title: Red House, Tuen Mun
geometryBasis: The existing two-storey Hung Lau in the February 2017 description, including the southeast verandah and attached two-storey rear kitchen and storeroom.
sectionBasis: The named native footprint and the original grade set the massing. The heritage appraisal identifies the pitched two-unit house, double verandah, pierced block balustrade and rear service annex.

frontVerandah.material: plastered brick, wood and screened panels

rearAnnex.roofAndHeights: eaves and shallow roof estimated from primary morphology

section.orientation: Southeast facing. The measured long façade runs northeast–southwest.
estimates: Architectural heights and the opening grid are approximate.
The lower finished level is estimated against a natural terrain grade that crosses the rear wall.
The documented hooded metal windows and varied plaster color establish appearance without using exterior photography.

limitations: The exterior follows the February 2017 heritage description and the twelve-point mapped outline. The map controls the house, verandah and rear projections.
Floor levels, roof pitch, window spacing, screen-block pattern and color are approximate interpretations of the written evidence.
The steep natural grade remains in its original source grid. Thresholds, footings and the short approach stairs use modeled elevations.
The reconstruction covers the standing house, verandah and attached service annex. The surrounding former farm is represented by the original terrain.
